All these steering commands end if you steer with the Steering Zone, click steer. or use > and < keys.
'High 7 Deg': Tack downwind 7 deg closer to the wind than normal. 'Low 7 Deg' is opposite.
Run Downwind: Sail the best angle for downwind progress. Manual steering ends this command.
'Jibe': Your boat jibes and assumes a course for good progress downwind. Not always visible.
'Reach': Your boat turns to a beam reach. This is a good command to duck a starboard tacker.
'Tack': Your boat tacks and assumes a closehauled course. Not visible when sailing downwind.
If you want to sail a normal closehauled course after using 'Pinch' of 'Foot', select 'Closehauled' again.
'Pinch': Your boat beats 5 deg closer to the wind than normal closehauled. Foot is the opposite.
'Closehauled' (Beat Button): Your boat beats to windward at a good angle to the wind. Ends if you steer.
> and < keys: Your boat turns 10 deg to starboard or port per press. ' key and Enter key also work.

Closehauled:
No other boat is interfering with your wind.
Clear air:
the farthest aft part of a boat ahead. The leading boat is 'clear ahead'.

Clear astern:
Your wind is blocked by another boat that is upwind.
Blanketed:
Sails with a lot of draft. A full shape.
Baggy sails:
Sailing as close as possible, with good speed, into the wind.
Beating:
Turn the boat away from the wind.
Bear off:
Your wind is adversely affected by another boat.
Bad air:
Wind deflected by a boat ahead when closehauled. Your pointing is poorer.
Backwinded:
Wind shifting to your left as you face it. A counterclockwise shift.
Backing wind:
Wind perceived while sailing: a combination of true wind and the motion of the boat.
Apparent wind:
Directly to the side of the boat.

Leeward boat:
Away from the wind. A boat's leeward side is the side where her mainsail lies.
Leeward:

Imaginary lines from a mark ending a beat or a run. A closehauled boat on a
Laylines:
A wind shift toward the bow.
Header:
To turn the boat toward the wind. Also called 'luffing'.
Head up:
When beating, to bear off a little lower to gain speed.
Foot:
Distance to windward to the nearest land.
Fetch:
Almost no draft (flat like a board).
Flat sails:
Curvature of a sail surface (camber).
Draft:
The weight of the boat.
Displacement:
To leeward. Also, a leg of the race with the wind from aft of abeam.
Downwind:
When beating or tacking downwind, to pass ahead of a competitor.
Cross:
- GLOSSARY -    page 2
Sailing with the wind from roughly abeam. Not beating or running.
Reach:
Sailing with the wind blowing from the port side.
Port tack:
To your left when facing the bow.
Port:
When beating, the angle sailed from the wind.
Point:
When beating, to sail so close to the wind that speed is sacrificed.
Pinch:
Buoy end of a start or finish end. Opposite of Committee Boat end.
Pin end:
A wind shift that does not swing back on a leg.
Persistent shift:
A wind that shifts back and forth during the same leg.
Oscillating wind:
To sail outside (beyond) the laylines.
Overstand:
Two boats 'overlap' when neither is clear astern. They are side by side.
Overlap:
A wind direction indicator at the top of the mast.
Masthead fly:
flaps like a flag. Also, to turn the boat toward the wind.
Reducing the angle of the sail to the wind so that it partially
Luff:
A wind shift away from the bow.
Lift:
The part of a race course from one mark to the next.
Leg:

A race course with only beats and runs.
Windward/Leeward:
The end of a starting line off the windward side of a starboard tack boat.
Windward end:
An overlapped boat on the other's windward side.
Windward boat:
The side of the boat from which the wind blows.
Windward:
Wind shifting to your right as you face it. A clockwise shift.
Veering wind:
Toward the wind.
Upwind:
Wind perceived by a stationary observer such as on the Committee Boat.
True wind:
Sailing a zig zag course on a run to increase the boat's speed.
Tacking downwind:
Sailing with the wind blowing from the starboard side.
Starboard tack:
To your right when facing the bow.
Starboard:
The line (rope) that controls in and out movement of a sail.
Sheet:
The distance between two boats.
Separation:
where sailing the rhumbline would be below best tacking downwind angle.
Sailing with the wind from roughly astern. Also, a leg of the race course
Run:
A straight line from one mark to the next.
